messages.author: 7b36a5521b8eb4d4
messages.subject: Store Data Beyond Application Instances
parts:
I read that data written by an application to the local filesystem of an instance will be lost when the app is re-deployed. The application I'm writing allows users to submit some new data to the application and compare it to the existing data. The new data should be saved with the existing data, so that the dataset can grow as users make submissions and remain in the dataset if the server is restarted. It's basically a data frame that grows when users submit new results. What alternative method is there to achieve this ?

Also, the webpage states "By default, shinyapps.io deploys all applications on ‘medium’ instances", but the table below has small instances shown as the default.

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Store Data Beyond Application Instances
parts:
Hi Dario,
You may want to check out an article we just got posted on our articles list yesterday.
At this time shinyapps.io does not have persistent storage (although we are considering adding that in the near future).  With an append only model you might be okay, but it is probably worth reading the article and seeing whether something like using Google sheets might be a better way to capture your survey data.

http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/persistent-data-storage.html

Best,
Tareef

Maybe a short question on something that the article mentioned above does not answer:

Does Shiny Server support file system storage across sessions? (I am pretty sure it does, but would be nice to hear an official statement from RStudio on this. Thank you!)

My intention would then be to setup my own instance of Shiny Server, so that I can let users of an app read/write on files continuously from the server file system.
